title: Moving ramp relay
summary: An orange ball rests in the left Panda's cup, and the right Panda holds a straight channel that is open at both ends. The left arm must pass the ball into the inlet part of the channel. The ball must then leave the channel by its outlet end and be caught again in free flight by the left cup. The relay is then repeated with the channel held at a clearly different orientation from the first time. After the second catch, the left cup must deliver the ball into a fixed basin, where it must come to rest.
robot_setup: panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). It carries an open-top square cup, 0.14 m x 0.14 m inside (2 x `tool_half`, `tool_half` = 0.07 m), with four 0.055 m high, 5 mm thick walls and a 5 mm floor, held by an adapter on its tool -x wall. The tool frame is the centre of the cup floor's inner surface, z up. The TCP sits 0.12 m along tool -x and 0.04 m above the tool frame. Start: (-0.04, -0.14, 0.23), orientation identity (upright). panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). It carries a straight channel, open at both ends and 0.28 m long (2 x `right_tool_half`, `right_tool_half` = 0.14 m). It has a flat floor 72 mm wide and 8 mm thick and two side walls 40 mm high and 8 mm thick. A side adapter holds it at the middle of its tool +y wall. The tool frame is the centre of the floor's top surface: x runs along the channel (the +x end is the outlet, the -x half the inlet side), y across it, z up. The TCP sits 0.12 m along tool -x, 0.12 m along tool +y and 0.04 m above the tool frame. Start: (0.18, 0.10, 0.24), quaternion (0, 0, 0, 1) (yawed 180 deg: level, outlet end toward world -x). Role labels (panda-0 / panda-1) by phase: first_channel_entry donor / channel_operator; first_moving_exit relocating_receiver / moving_outlet; first_catch catcher / channel_support; second_channel_entry donor / changed_channel; second_moving_exit relocating_receiver / moving_outlet; second_catch_and_delivery catcher_deliverer / channel_support.
scene: An orange ball (radius 18 mm) rests at a slightly random spot on the floor of the left arm's cup. A fixed blue open-top basin, 0.15 m x 0.15 m inside and 0.06 m deep, stands on posts above the table. Nothing moves by itself; once the ball is in the channel, it rolls under gravity. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Ball: radius `radius` = 0.018 m, mass `object_mass` = 0.035 kg, restitution 0.08, friction 0.2. At reset it is placed at rest at the left cup's frame origin + (u_x, u_y, `radius` + 0.0005) in world axes, i.e. 0.5 mm above the cup floor. u_x and u_y are drawn uniformly in [-`ball_offset`, `ball_offset`] = [-0.015, 0.015] m. `ball_roll_speed` = 0, so the ball starts at rest and no heading is drawn. Basin: static container with floor top surface centre at (0.04, -0.24, 0.08); inner half-size 0.075 x 0.075 m; wall height 0.06 m (rim at z = 0.14); friction 0.4; restitution 0.03. Cup: `tool_half` = 0.07, `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg. Channel: `right_tool_half` = 0.14, `right_tool_mass` = 0.25 kg. Both tools have `tool_friction` = 0.3 and restitution 0.05. `outlet_min_speed` = 0 (see static_outlet_exit). Horizon `horizon` = 25 s. The only random draws are u_x and u_y, made at reset.

phases.name: first_channel_entry
phases.text: The ball touches the channel (any part of panda-1's tool) while two things hold. Its centre is more than 0.045 m from the channel centre on the inlet side (channel-frame x < -0.045). And at that moment it does not touch the cup. The channel's pose (position and orientation) at that moment is recorded.

phases.name: first_moving_exit
phases.text: The ball's centre is more than 0.13 m from the channel centre on the outlet side (channel-frame x > 0.13, i.e. within 1 cm of the outlet end or past it; y and z are not bounded), while the ball does not touch the channel. At that moment the world speed of the channel's outlet tip must be at least `outlet_min_speed`, which is 0 at this instance.

phases.name: first_catch
phases.text: The ball enters the left cup from above and is retained. The entry: after touching nothing for at least 0.025 s, the ball's centre passes downward through the plane 0.073 m above the cup floor (wall height 0.055 m + radius 0.018 m, in the cup's frame). At that crossing the centre must be within 0.052 m (`tool_half` - radius) of the cup centre along both cup x and cup y. From then on the ball must stay contained in the cup for 0.18 s without interruption. Contained in the cup means all of the following, in the cup's frame: |x| and |y| of the ball centre below 0.0619 m (`tool_half` - 0.45 x radius); height above the cup floor between 0.014 m and 0.0528 m; in contact with the cup within the last 25 ms; moving at less than 0.09 m/s relative to the cup (including the cup's rotation). The free-flight time counts only from the start of this phase.

phases.name: second_channel_entry
phases.text: As in first_channel_entry, the ball touches the channel at channel-frame x < -0.045 while not touching the cup. In addition, the channel's orientation must differ by at least 0.30 rad (about 17.2 deg) from the orientation recorded at the first entry, i.e. |q . q_first| <= cos 0.15 for the unit quaternions. A touch while the orientation is too close to the first one does not count.

phases.name: second_moving_exit
phases.text: As in first_moving_exit: the ball's centre is at channel-frame x > 0.13 while the ball does not touch the channel, and the outlet tip moves at least `outlet_min_speed` (0 here).

phases.name: second_catch_and_delivery
phases.text: First the ball is caught again in the left cup exactly as in first_catch. That is: an entry after at least 0.025 s of free flight (counted from the start of this phase) through the plane 0.073 m above the cup floor within 0.052 m of the centre on both axes, then contained in the cup for 0.18 s without interruption. After that catch, the ball must be contained in the basin and not touch the cup, for 0.7 s without interruption. Contained in the basin means all of the following, in the basin's frame (origin at the centre of its floor's top surface, axes = world axes): |x| and |y| of the ball centre below 0.0669 m (0.075 - 0.45 x radius); height above the basin floor between 0.014 m and 0.0578 m; in contact with the basin within the last 25 ms; speed below 0.09 m/s. This completes the task.

task_failures: static_outlet_exit: when the ball meets the first_moving_exit or second_moving_exit condition, the world speed of the channel's outlet tip is below `outlet_min_speed`. The outlet tip is the tool-frame point (`right_tool_half`, 0, 0). At this instance `outlet_min_speed` = 0, so this failure cannot occur.
contact_rules: The cup and the channel may touch only the ball. They must not touch each other, the basin or its posts, the table or the robot pedestals. No other robot part, the fingers included, may touch anything. The two arms and their tools must never touch each other, so the ball has to pass between cup and channel without the two tools touching. A tool must not touch its own arm.
world_goals_fixed: All phase geometry is relative to the channel, the cup and the basin.
world_goals_seeded: `goal_target` = (0.18, 0.10, 0.24), the channel's start position, is announced at reset, but no phase condition uses it.
difficulty_note: Each relay hands the ball from cup to a hand-held channel. The ball then rolls out by itself, and the same cup that gave it away has to catch it in free flight off the outlet. The second relay must use a channel orientation at least 0.30 rad different from the first, and the basin delivery counts only after the second catch has been held.
standard_notes: Nothing moves at t = 0: the ball rests in the left cup. Once the ball is in the channel it rolls on its own toward whichever end is lower, and it leaves the outlet within moments.
